marks.gloss_en: הכא נמי, איכא ניצויי אביו וניצויי רבו -- here too [as with honour at 24a.17], there is the quarrelling of his father and of his teacher
מאי טעמא — חיישינן שמא מינות נזרקה בו: the reason he may not pass even in white
מאי טעמא — חיישינן שמא מינות נזרקה בו: the reason he may not pass even barefoot
what is the reason? we are concerned that perhaps heresy has been cast into him
one who says 'I will not pass before the ark in coloured [garments]' -- he may not pass even in white
one who makes his tefillin round -- [it is a] danger
ערום מאי טעמא לא -- משום כבוד צבור, הכא נמי -- the naked minor's reason applies to the minor pocheach
then ask about a naked [minor]! why may a naked one not [read]? because of the honour of the congregation
a minor whose limbs are exposed may not read from the Torah (asked by Ulla bar Rav, affirmed by Abaye)
a priest who has blemishes on his hands may not lift his hands [in the priestly blessing]
תניא נמי הכי: ידיו בוהקניות לא ישא את כפיו
it was taught: the blemishes they spoke of -- on his face, his hands and his feet
תניא נמי הכי: אין מורידין לפני התיבה לא אנשי בית שאן ולא אנשי בית חיפה ולא אנשי טבעונין, מפני שקורין לאלפין עיינין ולעיינין אלפין
Rav Asi: a Haifan or a Beit-Shean-ite may not lift his hands
תניא נמי הכי: זבלגן לא ישא את כפיו
ואם היה דש בעירו מותר -- the same baraita's second clause bears out the answer
והא ההוא דהוה בשיבבותיה דרב הונא, והוה פריס ידיה! -- a zavlegan in Rav Huna's own neighbourhood lifted his hands
ההוא דש בעירו הוה -- that one was familiar in his town (= p_huna_hahu_dash_beiro)
Rav Huna: a zavlegan [one whose eyes run] may not lift his hands
תניא נמי הכי: סומא באחת מעיניו לא ישא את כפיו
ואם היה דש בעירו מותר -- the same baraita's second clause bears out the answer
והא ההוא דהוה בשיבבותיה דרבי יוחנן דהוה פריס ידיה! -- one blind in one eye in R' Yochanan's own neighbourhood lifted his hands
ההוא דש בעירו הוה -- that one was familiar in his town (= p_yochanan_hahu_dash_beiro)
R' Yochanan: one blind in one of his eyes may not lift his hands
R' Chiyya to R' Shimon bar Rebbi: were you a Levite, you would be disqualified from the platform, because your voice is thick
כרבי יוסי, דתניא... -- the blind man's torch: people see him and save him
and the Rabbanan: he does have benefit, as R' Yosei
אמרו לו לרבי יהודה: הרבה צפו לדרוש במרכבה ולא ראו אותה מימיהם -- the Sages' argument to R' Yehuda
many have contemplated expounding the Chariot and never in their lives saw it
אמרו לו לרבי יהודה: הרבה צפו לדרוש במרכבה ולא ראו אותה מימיהם -- the Sages' argument to R' Yehuda
ורבי יהודה: התם באובנתא דליבא תליא מילתא... הכא משום הנאה הוא, והא לית ליה הנאה (= p_merkava_ovanta_deliba, p_meorot_mishum_hanaa, p_suma_lait_lei_hanaa)
there [the Chariot] the matter depends on the understanding of the heart, and he concentrates and knows

until an incident came my way: once I was walking in the dead of night and darkness, and I saw a blind man walking on the road with a torch in his hand; I said to him: my son, why do you need this torch?

לימא תנינא להא דתנו רבנן: shall we say the mishna's 'round -- no mitzva in it' already teaches that tefillin must be square (and, with Rava, at seams and diagonals)? (no support kind names תנינא; dika_nami follows chullin_13a)
the mishna: one who makes his tefillin round -- [it is a] danger
אמר רב פפא: מתניתין דעבידא כי אמגוזא -- the mishna speaks of tefillin made like a nut, so it does not teach the baraita (= p_rav_pappa_amguza)
Rav Pappa: our mishna is [about tefillin] made like a nut
it was taught: if most of the people of the town have this as their work, it is permitted
